column1: # How people actually type Urdu in Latin letters, and what they mean by it.
# Nothing here is reachable from the phonetic rules, because Urdu's own script
# throws away what the rules would need:
#  - short vowels, which it does not write at all, so only a dictionary knows
#    whether an "a" is a long ا or nothing ("kitab" is کتاب but "karna" کرنا);
#  - the retroflex row ("roti" is روٹی, "bara" بڑا) and the Arabic letters Urdu
#    keeps for its loanwords ("khas" is خاص, "zaroori" ضروری, "galat" غلط);
#  - a final ہ against a final ا ("bacha" is بچہ, "karna" کرنا);
#  - the nasalisation ں, which is grammar rather than sound ("hain" is ہیں,
# Chat shorthand is here too, the kind that drops letters wholesale: "k" for کہ,
# "h" for ہے, "nhi" for نہیں, "kr" for کر, "bht" for بہت.
# This list matters more than its Bengali or Hindi twin: Urdu ships no bundled
# word list, and the downloadable one is flat — every word in it has frequency
# 1 — so these lines are both the vocabulary and the only ranking the layout has
# until the user downloads a list. The commonest spellings were taken from the
# `ur_rom` frequency list (Pakistani social-media text) and the Urdu written by
# hand; it is a draft and wants an Urdu speaker's review (issue #496).
# Format: spelling<TAB>urdu   (one mapping per line; # starts a comment)
# A spelling may repeat to offer several forms, most-preferred first.
